claims.text: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs is primarily governed by Al-induced chemical short-range ordering.
Al-induced short-range ordering lowers the local free energy.
Al-induced short-range ordering suppresses deleterious phase transformations.
Suppression of phase transformations enables retention of high-temperature strength.
Suppression of phase transformations enables retention of environmental resistance.
Suppression of phase transformations enables retention of radiation tolerance.
Suppression of phase transformations enables retention of cryogenic toughness.
Increasing Al within an appropriate composition window promotes short-range ordering without producing long-range intermetallic order.
Al favors partially ordered local atomic arrangements in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
The locally ordered arrangements impede nucleation and growth of intermetallic phases.
The locally ordered arrangements impede nucleation and growth of carbide precipitates.
Al-induced local order increases resistance to phase decomposition during thermal cycling and extreme-environment exposure.
A moderately higher-Al alloy will exhibit more pronounced short-range order than an identically processed low-Al alloy.
A moderately higher-Al alloy will decompose more slowly and exhibit reduced precipitation kinetics during aging.
A moderately higher-Al alloy will retain greater high-temperature strength than the low-Al baseline.
A moderately higher-Al alloy will exhibit better oxidation resistance than the low-Al baseline.
A moderately higher-Al alloy will exhibit greater cryogenic toughness than the low-Al baseline.
Outside the proposed Al-content window, long-range ordered intermetallic phases or different transformation pathways may govern behavior.
The quantitative relationship between short-range order and multi-environment mechanical-property retention has not been established.
